assumptions: Agent-assisted draft. Human semantic review is incomplete; no model outputs were used to author these inputs. Gold describes fictional states, not measured beliefs in an independent reader model.

Four wording/entity templates fully cross initial reader location belief I, exact message location M, sender-trusted receipt B, and current world W, with both global physical-name mappings: 128 distinct sender inputs.

Each sender input has two private actual-delivery A records, giving 256 fictional rows. A is never included in a sender-visible message. A pairs have identical inputs; they are not independent model observations.
Gold for the fixed place_b proposition: sender-attributed reader belief T = M if B else I; actual reader belief R = M if A else I; world = W.

I is independent of M. The prospectively primary I!=M subset has 64 unique sender inputs (32 mapping-paired factor/template cells). I=M supplies 64 receipt-invariance controls; its attribution does not depend on B.
I-only and M-only label rules each reach 75% on all 128 inputs and 50% on the primary I!=M subset. W-only and B-only rules reach 50% on both subsets.
A hidden-actual-reader prediction can achieve at most 75% across all A-paired rows, and exactly 50% on I!=M. R is identifiable without A when I=M.

Each template crosses every factor independently, removing the earlier wording/record-polarity association. Templates still differ in names and places as well as wording and share one conditional-update reasoning family.
Mapping swaps exchange complete physical names globally; they are paired lexical controls, not independent scenarios or complementary questions.

The old neutral system and exact nested slot-b question are reused. Story capture includes the candidate proposition but no perspective question. Both captures end with the model's normal assistant-generation header.

The sender knows the actual world but attributes beliefs according to its trusted receipt, including when the reader accepts a false location claim. Possible receipt error and A are not disclosed to the sender.
The message is fixed and sent by a location service. No sender-generated report, incentive manipulation, omission or unknown future belief is tested.

No new probe fitting, threshold/layer selection or calibration uses this bank. Before/after transfer localizes a fixed readout; failure before the question does not prove the model lacks a belief representation.

messages.content: Read the fictional scene. Questions will follow. Each person has only the observations and messages explicitly available to them. People remember the last place they observed the token and update after seeing a move or receiving a trusted message about its current place. They do not infer an unobserved move. Narrator-only information is not shared with a character merely because the narrator describes it.

At 09:00, Daria and Lennox inspect the token together inside the amber strongbox. Each sees the other complete this inspection. Daria believes the token is in the amber strongbox, and Lennox knows this.

After 09:00, Daria has no direct observation of the token and no location evidence except this one possible service message. If the message is fully read, the reader accepts its stated location and replaces the initial location belief, even if the message is false. If no message or notification arrives, the reader retains the initial location belief. Lennox knows these update rules.

At 09:03, Lennox's private live camera shows the token in the amber strongbox. That view is accurate and unavailable to Daria.

At 09:05, a location service attempts to transmit this exact text to Daria: "The token is now in the amber strongbox." Lennox can inspect the outgoing text but cannot observe whether it arrives or is read.

At 09:10, Lennox receives a delivery receipt stating: Neither the 09:05 message nor a notification of it reached Daria. Lennox accepts this particular receipt as definitive evidence of whether Daria read the message. Lennox has no other delivery evidence and cannot independently check delivery.

The scene ends at 09:20. The token has stayed at its 09:03 location since that camera check. There have been no further observations, messages, receipts or conversations. No direct observation or independent delivery account is available to Lennox.

Candidate proposition: "The token is in the teal strongbox." This is a statement to assess, not new evidence or a message received by either person.

End of account. A question may follow.

Question: At the end of the scene, does Lennox think that Daria believes that the token is in the teal strongbox? Answer only YES or NO.
